Commentary.Commentary: The visitors have close to 35 minutes to bat before Lunch. A wicketless period will be the only thing on their minds. Meanwhile, given that the conditions are overcast, Boult and Southee will be licking their lips. Stay tuned...

West Indies will feel a little bit frustrated as they had a chance to roll the Kiwis over for 325 or below. But overall, they will be pleased with their comeback, after being wayward with the first new ball. Gabriel managed to pick 4 wickets while Roach was better this morning, with 3 scalps.

The Kiwis will be happy with their efforts. From one point of view, you could argue that they were 154/1 at one stage and should have reached 500. But having been asked to bat first, they will take this total. Starts for every batsman in the top 8 indicate that the pitch is not the easiest to bat on. Raval was unlucky to miss out on a century after holding the innings together for so long.

End of an entertaining stand. The Southee-Boult blitzkrieg has given the Kiwis more than an upper hand in this Test. The Windies started very well this morning, getting rid of Wagner and Blundell quickly but just could not do the finishing job.

OUT! Caught and bowled! The innings ends at last. Banged in short outside off, Southee backs away and attempts to slap it over the bowler but toe-ends it towards him. Roach is alert this time and takes the catch inches above the turf. The 61-run stand is broken and NEW ZEALAND ARE FINALLY BOWLED OUT FOR 373.
A slower ball, fuller in length, down the leg side, Southee is foxed as he is early into his flick. Is hit on the pads and Roach starts to appeal but then bails out.
Outside off, left alone.
Landed wide outside off, Trent shows the bat in a high angle, as if to leave it but then brings it down to dab the ball to the off side.
Flighted outside off, Boult comes down the track but is comprehensively beaten in the flight. However, he composes himself and does not go through with the shot. Jumps back in the crease.
A long hop, wide outside off, heaved over Boult to long on for a single.

NOT OUT. Just wasting a bit of time. Fuller and flighted outside off, Southee has a wild swing but misses. The back foot just comes out of the crease for a bit but is back in by the time Dowrich can affect a stumping. Replays confirm.
Stumping appeal! Something out of nothing. Brathwaite is not sure but Dowrich reckons he has Southee stumped here... referred upstairs.
Landed wide outside off, Southee watches it go past.
Kraigg Brathwaite to have a bowl now.
Boult makes room to play another inventive shot and Roach bowls it outside off. The batsman has a flash at it but misses.
Fullish delivery, clipped with the angle to the leg side for a single.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.

Should have taken that! Slower delivery on a fullish length on off, Boult perhaps doesn't spot the change in pace. He chips it straight back to Roach. The bowler is late to react and the ball goes past over his hands. Rolls towards long off and a single is taken.
Dug in short around off, Boult sways away from the line of the delivery.
Bowls this one well outside off, Boult doesn't fish at it.
Drills this one down the ground for a run.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
SIX! Clean as a whistle! No respite for the Windies from both ends. Slow through the air around off, Southee puts his skates on and lifts it over cow corner and the ball sails over the fence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Pushes this one against the spin to covers.
FOUR! Starts off with a short delivery outside off, ample time for Southee to rock back and flay it through point for a boundary.
Time for Drinks. Meanwhile, after all the lusty blows that the pace bowlers received, Roston Chase is brought into the attack.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. 14 from the over.
FOUR! Tonked! Boult is dealing in boundaries. Full length ball on off, he backs away and hits it hard over the bowler for a one-bounce boundary. Moves to 35 from 18 balls.

SIX! Boult is playing in the T20 mode! Amazing ball-striking from him. Gets a short delivery in his arc and absolutely clobbers it over long on for a maximum. Gabriel is leaking runs, the frustration for the visitors continues.
Boult makes room again, then shuffles across to the off side. Gabriel bowls it down the leg side and Boult misses his tuck.
FOUR! Whack! Boult makes room and Gabriel instead of following him bowls a back of a length ball around off. The No. 11 cuts it through the point region to pick up another boundary.
Boult makes room as he has been doing on a regular basis. Gabriel bangs it short and the No. 11 rises on his toes to block it.
Down the leg side, Tim misses his whip shot.
Around the hips, tucked past short leg for a run.
Makes room to play another inventive shot but misses.
Dowrich has a chat with Cummins. These runs will surely be hurting the visitors.

FOUR! Runs are flowing now! Boult has moved to 20 from 11 balls. Back of a length delivery around off, Boult flashes at it and gets the ball to meet at the center of the bat. The ball goes through the point region for another rocketing boundary.
FOUR! Dismissed from its presence! Good length delivery on off, Boult clears his front leg and whacks it aerially through covers. The ball reaches the fence like a tracer bullet.
Played to the point region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Makes room and plays it with an angled blade to point.
Almost took his partner out! Full length ball on middle, Southee hammers it past his partner to long on for a run. Boult almost fell in an effort to evade the hit.
The ball has gone out of the park with that mammoth six. The fourth umpire brings in a replacement.

SIX! Going, going, gone! That came right off the screws. Gabriel tries to tuck Southee up with another short delivery but the lower order batsman is up to the task. Makes room and pulls it over long leg for a huge biggie! The partnership moves to 21 from 15 balls, this will surely frustrate the Windies.
Another bouncer, Southee goes for a pull but top edges it over the fielder at mid-wicket. It falls in no man's land and a brace is taken.
Short delivery, Tim goes for a full fledged hook but misses.
A long in place. Two more men in the deep at the leg side as well. Bouncer coming up...

That must have hurt! Full delivery on off, Southee bludgeons it down the track. Gabriel in his followthrough sticks his right foot out and takes a blow around the heel. He is in some pain as he bends down to gather himself up. Seems to be fine to continue.
Boult again makes room to play an expansive shot. Cummins follows him but it goes past the batsman to the keeper.
Backs away and drops it besides the pitch to scurry across to the other end.
Short delivery, Tim sways away of the line of the delivery.
Backs away to the good length delivery and plays it to covers for a quick single.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

SIX! How good is that shot! Back of a length delivery in line of the stump, Boult is expecting that and hence, sits on the back foot. Makes room and ramps it over the man at third man for a maximum. Makes good use of the short boundaries.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Backs away and hits it towards wide mid on to rotate strike.
FOUR! Cheeky! Good length delivery on middle, Boult arches back and ramps it over the slip cordon the find the fence.
Squared the tailender up completely. Back of a length ball on off, Boult gets into a bad position and tries to fend it off but gets it off the outer half to gully.
That's the perfect definition of a toe crusher - right on the boots, Boult stays leg side of the ball and jams it out.
Trent Boult is the last man in.

OUT! Timber! Fourth wicket for Shannon Gabriel. He has been breathing fire with the second new ball barring the overstepping issue. He pitches it on a good length around off and gets it to jag back in a touch after landing. Blundell is caught in his crease trying to keep it out but seems to have got an inside edge which goes onto disturb the timber behind. A resolute knock from the wicket-keeper batsman comes to an end. In fact, the replays show the ball brushed the bottom half of the bat and dislodged the middle stump.
Dug in short, ducked under and evaded.
A play and a miss! Back of a length delivery around off, nipping in. Southee goes for a half-hearted pull but gets beaten. That just went over the off stump.

In the air... but safe! Well-directed bouncer on middle, Blundell is not in a good position to play the pull shot but still goes through with it. The ball hits the high part of the willow and flies towards deep square leg. It falls right in the gap between the two fielders running across from either side. A run taken.
Good length ball outside off, Blundell lets it sail through to the keeper.
The weather has turned gloomy. Grey clouds are building up. There are some chances of rain today but let's hope it stays away.
Short of a length delivery, Southee absolutely smashes it past short leg for a run. The short leg fielder is always in the line of fire, tough position to be stationed at.
Fullish on middle and leg, tucked with soft hands to mid-wicket.
Miguel Cummins to bowl for the first time this morning.
Fuller in length at 145.6 clicks outside off, Blundell plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length delivery outside off, holding its line. Tom points his bat skywards to let it go. He has been very patient and resilient in this innings.
Continues to persist in the same channel outside off, it is on a good length. Tom camps back and defends it stoutly.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down. Full delivery down the leg side, Southee aims to clip it away but is hit on the pads. Gabriel puts in a belated appeal for an LBW but the umpire pays no heed. The batsmen sneak in a leg bye. Importantly, for New Zealand, Blundell is back on strike.
Short delivery on middle, sits up nicely for Southee. He smashes it straight to the man present at deep mid-wicket. A run taken.
Blundell has been so good in picking up those sharp single. Taps the good length delivery towards cover-point and calls his partner through for a swift single.
In the zone of apprehension, Tom lets it go on its way.
On a drivable length outside off, Blundell resists the temptation to go for an expansive shot and makes an assured leave.
FOUR! Sublime! Fractionally overpitched in line of the stumps, Blundell leans ahead and drives it crisply past the bowler. It speeds through the outfield and races to the long on fence.
Fuller length ball, angling in, kept out watchfully off the front foot.
Good game awareness! On a length around off, Blundell plays it with soft hands besides the pitch on the leg side and scurries through to the other end. A long, long over comes to an end.
Sits deep in the crease and blocks the good length delivery watchfully.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, pushed confidently off the front foot to mid on.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
No ball! Gabriel oversteps by a country mile, not a surprise. On middle and leg, clipped to the leg side for a single.

No ball! Gabriel's issues with overstepping continue. Short ball on middle and leg, Southee pulls it through mid-wicket for a run. It is literally waste of an effort, he needs to seriously work on this problem.
Another short delivery but this one is outside off, Tim ducks under it with ease.

Ooh... that's nasty! Bouncer on middle, Southee goes for a pull but the ball brushes his gloves and seems to have hit the grille of his helmet. He gets off-balanced but manages to keep himself from falling over on the wickets. That must have shaken him up.
On a length on leg stump, Southee whips it smartly to deep square leg for a run and will retain strike.

In the air... but safe! Good length delivery on off, Southee tries to turn it across but gets a leading edge. The ball balloons over the point region. The fielder from gully chases it and saves a couple for his side. The replays show that it came actually off the outside edge of the bat. Today's bats, I tell you...
Testing the tailender with a short one, he is equal to the task and ducks under it.
That's an ugly heave. Shortish on off, Southee plays an agricultural slog towards wide mid on.
Fullish delivery, nudged to mid-wicket to rotate strike.

Tight run! Southee hangs back and taps it besides the pitch on the off side. Takes off for a run and his partner responds. Roach is quick to attack to the ball but fumbles while trying to collect it. That allows Tim to make his ground safely.

Well bowled and equally well played! Full length ball, swinging in substantially. Tom stays well-balanced and clips it towards wide mid on. Chase dives to his right and makes a partial stop. Gets up and keeps it down to a brace.

FOUR! Compact and assured in strokeplay! Half volley on middle Blundell drives it gloriously down the ground and the ball whistles away to the fence. Look at his followthrough after playing the shot, supreme confidence.
Full length delivery at 144.6 clicks outside off, Blundell plants his front foot across and allows it through.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and answers it with a straight bat.
Gabriel misses his radar trying to bowl at quick pace. Slips this one down the leg side, Tom tries to glance it but misses.
Length delivery on middle, nipping in. Blundell rises on his toes to tuck it away but misses to get rapped on the thigh pads.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end.
Steep bounce again. On a shortish length around off, jagging in and climbing on Southee. He hops and fends it off down the track. A wicket maiden for Roach to kickoff proceedings.
In the corridor of uncertainty, holding its line. Southee doesn't fiddle with it.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Tim Southee strides out to bat.

OUT! What a ripper of a catch! This is as good a take you will ever see. Take a bow, Shai Hope. Roach steams in and bowls a full length delivery on middle, swinging away. Wagner tries to drive down the ground with minimal foot movement but gets a fat outside edge. The ball is really traveling towards gully. Hope stationed there dives full length to his left like a goalkeeper and takes a stunning one-handed catch. All his teammates encircle him and are absolutely elated! Ideal start to the day for the Windies.
Good length delivery on off, nipping away after pitching. Neil points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Starts off with a sharp delivery right on the money. Roach goes wide of the crease and hits the deck hard. Generates some steep bounce as well. Wagner hops and keeps it out.

We are ready for live action. Tom Blundell and Neil Wagner will continue their innings. The second new ball is only 7 overs old and the visitors will be striving to clean the tail up as quickly as possible. Kemar Roach to bowl first up this morning. Two slips and a short leg in place. Here we go...

The Kiwis have been good but in patches. Majority of their batsmen have been guilty of throwing their wickets away. However, their lower order can be efficient and add some handy runs. With Tim Southee returning in the ranks, the pace attack looks even more ominous now. Let's see which team comes out on top today...

When the visiting batsmen come out to bat, they need to be resilient and determined. They do not need to look back far to draw inspiration. After a thrashing in Birmingham, they had come out with flying colors in Headingley. The potential is there but it needs to be translated into consistent performances if they are to succeed at the highest level.

Clear blue skies welcome us at the Seddon Park in Hamilton. It was a fired up Shannon Gabriel with the second new ball who provided a couple of important breakthroughs to give the Windies some good momentum yesterday. Still, the job is yet not done for them. Keeping the home side under 350 will be what they will aiming for. Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the second and final Test match between New Zealand and West Indies.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Day 2 is poised nicely. Tom Blundell is still out there and looking solid. Remember, he shepherded the lower middle order smartly in the last game. Will the Kiwis be able to go past 350? Or will the Windies clean the tail up in a jiffy? Join us tomorrow to catch all the action at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous day). Till then, cheers!

The 76-run stand from 112 balls between Colin de Grandhomme and Mitchell Santner threatened to take the game away from the visitors but the second new ball did the trick for them. Gabriel bowled with fire at the fag end of the day and struck in quick succession to catch the home side in a tricky situation. The pitch did quicken up in the later half of the day and credit to the tourists for being on the money.

Tom Latham and Jeet Raval laid the ideal foundation for the hosts with a 65-run opening stand. Miguel Cummins was the one who bowled with aggression and made good use of the short ball to pick up the first two wickets. Williamson got off to a decent start but failed to make it count while Jeet Raval fell to a brute of a delivery from Shannon Gabriel, missing out on a ton.

An absorbing day of Test cricket comes to an end. The Windies will be the happier of the two sides heading into the dressing room with a flurry of wickets, four to be precise in the final session of the day. Agreed that they were carved away for 113 runs, with especially de Grandhomme being severe on them but they had the last laugh.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, Blundell covers the line and keeps it out safely to mid on. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Shortish delivery around off, Blundell has no trouble in watching it through to the keeper's gloves.
Angling into Blundell who tucks it off his hips to the leg side.
Fuller in length outside off, Tom lets it go.

FOUR! Not where he intended but he will take it. Back of a length delivery, angling into Blundell. He opens his bat face and looks to steer it square off the wicket on the off side. However, he gets it off the outer half in the gap through third slip and gully and the ball races to the third man fence.
Back of a length delivery, Blundell hangs back and defends it stoutly.
Peppering him with the short stuff, this time Wagner lets it go in an assured way. End of a testing over.
Sharp short delivery on off, Wagner drops his wrists and leaves it in an awkward manner.

Ooh... that's nasty! Short delivery on leg stump, Wagner is caught in a tangle. Looks to fend it off but the ball hits his shoulder and lobs behind to the keeper. Dowrich puts in a casual appeal but the umpire stays put. He thought that there might have been glove involved but the replays confirm there was none.
Sits deep in the crease and negotiates the pacy delivery with a solid defense.
Down the leg side, Neil tries to help it away but misses.
Dug in short, Wagner ducks under it.
FOUR! Glorious! Full length delivery, Blundell comes forward and drives it through mid on for a boundary. That was all about timing and grace.
On a length outside off, Blundell opts to leave it.
Overpitched outside off, driven crisply to sweeper cover for a brace.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total. Wagner is off the mark.
Ooh... Gabriel is on song! Bowls a full length ball around off, Wagner goes for a drive but is beaten all ends up by the away movement.
Neil Wagner strides out to bat. Tricky period for New Zealand.

OUT! Castled! Gabriel breaches the defense of another batsman. He is on a roll, always a pleasure to watch when he finds his rhythm. Gabriel goes wider of the crease and angles in a length delivery on off, keeps a bit low. De Grandhomme hangs back to keep it out but misses it completely to get his stumps shattered. Good passage of play for the Windies, they have fought back really well. In fact, the replays show there was an inside edge and that deflected the ball on to the leg stump. De Grandhomme falls after playing an enterprising knock. He would be disappointed to lose his wicket at the fag end of the day.
Straying on the pads, tucked around the corner for a single.
Overpitched outside off, a gorgeous looking drive but straight to the man at mid off.
Shaping in substantially once again, inside edged besides the pitch on the leg side for a swift single.
Tentative! Swinging in from a good length around off, Blundell takes a step forward gingerly and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Back of a length delivery, answered with a straight bat.
Angling in from outside off, Tom doesn't flirt with it.
No ball! Another overstepping takes place, this time by Roach. Full length delivery outside off, Blundell remains circumspect in approach.
Good length delivery in the zone of apprehension, shaping in a bit. Colin knows where his off stump is and leaves it alone.
Blundell is off the mark! Taps the back of the length delivery towards cover-point and scurries across to the other end.
In the zone outside off, zipping through. Tom plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
Full length delivery, shaping in prodigiously. Blundell has his bat and pad close together and blocks it in a defiant manner.
Poor shot! Shortish delivery outside off, Blundell goes for a pull but the ball passes under his bat.
Length delivery outside off, angling in. Blundell makes an assured leave.
Back of a length delivery around off, pushed off the back foot to covers.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Colin leaves it alone.

FOUR! Not in control completely but gets the desired result! Short delivery outside off, de Grandhomme goes for an aerial pull shot as he knows there is no protection at deep mid-wicket. The ball flies towards the same region and rolls to the fence.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Hangs back to the incoming good length delivery and blocks it nicely.
Length delivery outside off, played with an angled blade past point for a couple.
Kemar Roach to bowl from the other end.
Blundell continues to leave balls outside the off stumps and sees the over through. A wicket-maiden for Gabriel.
Another one outside off, third leave in a row.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Tom Blundell, fresh from a ton on his debut, replaces Mitchell Santner. Can he play another innings of substance lower down the order?

OUT! Bowled 'em! The sound of the timber is one which brings sheer joy to a fast bowler. The second new ball reaps dividends for the visitors. Gabriel steams in and bowls a full and fast accurate delivery. The pace is at 142.6 kph and Santner is sitting in his crease. He looks to drive down the ground without any foot movement. Always risky to do so and he misses it completely to see his off stump pegged back. He departed in a similar manner to Cummins in the first Test and he has been undone by pace again. The entertaining 76-run stand from 112 balls has been cut short.
Fullish delivery, kept out watchfully.
The second new ball is available and it has been taken straightaway. Shannon Gabriel to run in with it first up.
Hangs back to the shorter length delivery and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Continues to be quick, eased through covers for a run.
Short and flat, Colin rocks back and cuts it past point for a brace.
On a flat trajectory well outside off, de Grandhomme shuffles across and makes a leave.
Sharp bouncer on off, Santner sits underneath the bumper in a flash.
Back of a length ball, defended solidly off the back foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Testing Santner with another short one but the southpaw is cool as a cucumber and lets it go.
Sits deep in the crease to the back of the length delivery and answers it with a straight bat.
Dug in short around off, Santner ducks under it in a jiffy.

SIX! 2nd Test fifty for Colin de Grandhomme and he has brought it up in style! Goes on to lead the charts with the most number of maximums this year, leaving Jadeja behind. Quick and flat around off, on a shorter length. De Grandhomme picks up the length quickly and whips it over deep square leg for a maximum. This has been a run-a-ball innings from him. Truly well-deserved.
Hangs back and punches it to the bowler.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Stays back to this one and keeps it out.
Short outside off, gives ample time to de Grandhomme to place it towards deep point for a brace.
Stays back to the quick and flat delivery and blocks it.
Brathwaite is back on.
Shortish delivery, climbing up on Mitchell. He rises with the bounce and blocks it solidly.
Short delivery around the rib-cage area, trying to tuck Santer up with a leg gully in place. The southpaw moves inside the line and lets it go.
Length delivery outside off, Mitchell stays patient and allows it through.
Dug in short, Santner ducks under it.
Similar delivery, Colin pulls it nicely this time through backward square leg. Chase in the deep moves swiftly to his right, gets the timing of his slide ride and stops a couple for his side.

Nervy moment! The pitch has quickened up after Tea and this is the right ploy from Cummins. In the previous game, the Windies batsmen had fallen like nine pins to the short stuff. Though the hosts are better on the pull and hook, it is worth it to test them once in a while. Sharp bouncer on middle and leg, de Grandhomme goes for the hook shot but gets beaten.
Miguel Cummins is back on. He has been the standout bowler for the visitors so far. Needs to strike for his side.
Short of a length delivery, punched off the back foot to covers.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, eased off the front foot to mi on.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Fullish in length, defended solidly off the front foot.
Stays back to the good length delivery and blocks it with command.
FOUR! Supreme confidence! Fractionally overpitched around off, de Grandhomme leans ahead and strokes it past the non-striker for a majestic boundary. 250 comes up for the hosts.

SIX! Now Santner goes boom boom! These two are entertaining the crowd thoroughly. Skates down the track and smokes it over long on for a maximum. The wheels are coming off for the Windies. A lottery over for New Zealand, 19 from it.
Hangs back to the shorter length delivery and dead-bats it.
FOUR! Runs are coming thick and fast for the hosts. Full delivery outside off, Santner drills it through covers for a rocketing boundary.

Full delivery outside off, Santner drives it with an open bat face through point. The fielder chases it and keeps it down to a couple. With that, the 50-run stand comes up. It has been a breezy one so far. Good counter-attack from the duo.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.
SIX! Clean as a whistle! He has been brilliant with his use of his feet. Slow through the air, de Grandhomme dances down the track and dumps it over wide long on for a maximum, his third of the day.

Still 16 overs are left to be bowled and only one hour remains in the day's play taking in account the extra time. The Windies have been pretty slow with their over rate. Jason Holder has already faced a consequence due to it. Brathwaite needs to be careful.
Outside off, left alone.
Fullish delivery outside off, moving away. Mitchell doesn't fiddle with it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Reifer continues to catch Santner in a tangle. Gets this one to swing away from a fuller length outside off. Satner is guilty of playing away from his body and gets foxed.
On a length outside off, Santner lets it go on its course.

Reifer is generating good inward movement and is troubling Santner. Serves it on a length and gets it to angle in with the arm, Santner tries to tuck it across but gets an inside edge onto his pads. A polite inquiry for an LBW follows but there was clearly bat involved.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and eases it to deepish mid on for a quick single.
Quicker through the air outside off, Santner is sure that it will spin away and makes a confident leave.
Fraction short in line, Santner keeps his eyes on the ball till the last moment and cuts it with the spin to point.
Strides forward to the loopy delivery and blocks it right under his eyes.
Outside off, turning away. Left alone with composure.
Outside off, skidding off the deck. Santner leaves it alone.

FOUR! Streaky runs! Full length ball on off, seaming away after hitting the deck. De Grandhomme pushes at it with hard hands and gets a thick outside edge past the diving gully fielder. The ball races to the fence behind.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and answers it with a straight bat.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Fractionally overpitched around off, driven crisply off the front foot to mid off.

Fuller in length, tempting de Grandhomme to go for an expansive shot but he resists. He has been brilliant with his shot selection so far. Seems to be led by a compass when to go for his shots and when to adopt a circumspect approach.
On a length, leaving the right-hander. He plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Drinks break.
Hangs back to the shorter delivery and keeps it out.
On a flatter trajectory, punched to mid on for a swift single.

SIX! 14 from the last 3 deliveries. He was scoring freely against Chase in the previous game and he has decided to play that way again. Fullish delivery outside off, de Grandhomme gets under it and extends his arms to whack it over covers. Such is the connection that it sails over the deep extra cover fence. He is growing in stature.
SIX! De Grandhomme is showing his colours now. Aggressive intent suits him and he is coming out with flying colours. Skips down the track once again and heaves it over cow corner for a biggie.
FOUR! Nicely done! Tossed up delivery, de Grandhomme chips down the track and lifts it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Fullish delivery, driven with the angle to mid on.
In the zone outside off, left alone. End of a testing over from Reifer.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, angling in. Santner fishes at it and is beaten again.
That's a peach! In the zone of apprehension, shaping in. Santner has no option but to play at it and gets foxed.

A chirpy appeal for an LBW is denied! Good length delivery, angling in substantially. Santner tries to tuck it across but gets hit on the pads. An appeal ensues but the umpire stays unmoved. Might be going down leg. The Hawk Eye confirms so.

Is that dropped? From the body language of the Windies players, seems like it is  a chance gone down. Pushed a bit quicker through the air outside off, de Grandhomme comes forward gingerly to account for the turn but there is only a fraction of it on offer. Ends up getting off-balanced and his right foot goes up in the air for a while as the ball goes past the outside edge of his bat. Dowrich behind the stumps fails to collect it and the ball rolls towards the leg side. Might have been a missed stumping chance as well. The Snickometer doesn't show any spike. The all-rounder survives.
Walks a couple of steps down the track and eases it through wide mid off for a run.
Coming in with the arm, tucked with the angle to mid-wicket.
Straighter one this time, outside off. Santner has his stumps covered and lets it go through safely.
Fullish delivery, de Grandhomme whips it past the left side of  the diving short mid-wicket fielder for an easy single.
Starts off with a low full toss from around the wicket and bowls it around off. Santner clears his front leg and milks it down to long off to rotate strike.
Time for spin again. Roston Chase is brought back for another spell.
Back of a length ball around off, punched firmly off the back foot to covers.
Reifer loses his radar this time. Slips it around the hips, Colin tucks it to fine leg for a brace.

Reifer has a spring in his stride now. The pitch has quickened up and he is making good use of it. Steams in and hits the deck hard around the off stump channel. De Grandhomme lifts his bat skywards and watches the ball sail through to the keeper.
Fullish in length, straighter line, blocked watchfully.
Tight line and length induces a false stroke. On a length around off, moving away just a touch after pitching. De Grandhomme pokes at it and is beaten all ends up.
On a drivable length outside off, urging de Grandhomme to go for a drive. The all-rounder resists the temptation and allows it through.
Slower delivery on a fullish length, Santner strides forward confidently and blocks it.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, Mitchell hangs back and pats it towards mid on.
Erring towards the leg stumpish line, tucked with ease towards the man stationed in front of square on the leg side.

FOUR! Hit with command! Shortish delivery in line of the stumps, Santner is sitting on the back foot expecting this length. It sits up nicely for him and he whacks it through straightish mid-wicket to find the ropes. 200 up for New Zealand.
Similar delivery, same shot, same result.
On a length, leaving the southpaw. He makes good use of the depth of the crease and blocks it solidly.

FOUR! Up and over! De Grandhomme had been patient in approach to all the length deliveries earlier. Gets one full in the zone outside off and frees his arm. Lifts it nonchalantly over covers for a glorious boundary.
Good length delivery, leaving the all-rounder. He points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Similar length delivery, kept out watchfully.
Third leave in a row. De Grandhomme continues to be circumspect in approach as he dosen't fiddle with a length delivery outside off.
Another friendly warning given by Rod Tucker to Reifer. He has been tantalizingly close to the danger area. The debutant needs to be careful.
In the channel outside off, de Grandhomme lets it go again.
Wide outside off, angling away. Colin leaves it alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Brilliant effort! Half volley outside off, Santner drives it exquisitely towards covers where Ambris dives full length to his right and stops a certain boundary. His effort is lauded by his teammates.
No ball! And Gabriel's love affair with overstepping continues. He is ahead of the popping crease by a country mile. Dug in short, Santner ducks under it.

No ball! This is the fourth time that Gabriel has overstepped. It continues to haunt him. Shortish delivery around the rib-cage area, Santner half-pulls it towards short leg who reacts quickly to his left but the ball goes past him through square leg. Two runs taken.
Similar delivery, driven crisply towards Cummins at mid on who is standing ahead of his usual position. He dives to his left and makes a partial stop to parry it towards mid off. A run taken.
Fullish delivery attacking the stumps, de Grandhomme leans a touch forward and taps it to mid on.
On a good length around off, punched firmly off the back foot to covers.
Good judgement! Back of a length ball around off, Santner plays it with soft hands past the bowler. Calls for a single immediately and gets the desired result.
Umpire Tucker just has a quiet word with Reifer in his followthrough. Not quite the official warning, but he is definitely treading on the danger area.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
On middle and off, angling in, solidly defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Full again, driven straight to mid off.
Fuller in length, just around off, watchfully kept out.
Outside off, allowed to go through.
Full and wide outside off, driven straight to cover.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Landed outside off, angling away, not played at.
Full and down the leg side, Santner misses his tuck and the ball rolls off his pads down the leg side. Dowrich dives to his right to stop.
Pitched outside leg and angling away, shouldered arms to.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
SHANNON GABRIEL is back on. Windies need to build on this momentum.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, played straight to point.
COLIN DE GRANDHOMME walks in now, at number 7, replacing Nicholls. The last time he batted for the Kiwis, he just tore the Windies apart with a breathtaking ton.

OUT! The decision stays! Big moment in the game and a massive chance for the visiting side. MAIDEN INTERNATIONAL WICKET for Reifer. He lands this on a length around off and gets it to nip back in. Nicholls is beaten by pace as he looks to defend and is hit on the pads. Reifer appeals, umpire Tucker thinks for a while and then raises his finger! Nicholls has a long look at the pitch, walks across to his partner and then signals the 'T' for the review. Hawk Eye shows the ball to be clipping the top of the leg stump. New Zealand do not lose a review but Nicholls is a goner. His feet were not to the pitch of the ball. Windies sense something now...
Nicholls has been adjudged LBW! He has reviewed it though. Does not seem to be an inside edge as the review was not instantaneous.
Back of a length outside off, Nicholls pushes it to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
RAYMON REIFER is into the attack again.
Hops and works this towards the off side for a quick run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Outside off, punched to the off side.
Now Santner is away. Works this length ball past short leg and runs across to the other end.
Short and way down the leg side, Santner lets it through.
Taps this through square leg and gets off strike. First single in 21 balls.
On a good length in line of the stumps, blocked back to the bowler.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
No idea about that one. Roach pitches this around middle and then gets it to deviate away. Mitchell looks to work it to the leg side but gets a leading edge to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A length ball around leg, Santner gets right behind that one to defend.
Landed around middle, angling away, left alone.
Now he tries to tuck this around the corner and gets hit on the pads.
Full and around off, Nicholls looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
A hat-trick of leaves outside off with that.
Fuller and wider outside off, let through again.
Outside off, left alone.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
Full and wide outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A length ball around middle, watchfully defended.
MITCHELL SANTNER walks in at number 6, replacing Taylor. Two southpaws in the middle.

OUT! Caught behind and Windies have a wicket immediately after Tea! Poor shot from Taylor. Very loose. He was flashing before Tea and has now flashed again after the break. On that occasion, he did not edge it. This time he did. The ball was short, yes, but not that wide to be cut. Taylor ended up being too close to the ball and got a thick outside edge. Dowrich fumbled behind but took it in the second attempt.
On a length outside off, watchfully defended.

ALMOST A WICKET! Great athleticism by Reifer. He keeps this full and Nicholls drives this straight back. Henry wants a run and is a couple of steps down the track but Reifer stops it in his followthrough and then has a shy at the striker's end, only to miss. Replays show it would have been touch and go!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! CLOUT! No half measures. New Zealand are going after the bowling. Short and wide outside off, Nicholls cracks it through cover-point and gets a boundary. Moves to 11 from 10 balls.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly through the covers. The ball stops before it reaches the ropes and three runs are taken.
Down the leg side, nudged fine for a single. The stand moves to 20 from just 24 balls.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
RAYMON REIFER to bowl from the other end.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! CLUNK! This time he does not miss out. Short and wide outside off, Taylor stays leg side of the ball and crashes it behind point for a boundary!
A length ball outside off, pretty wide, Taylor slashes but misses.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A short ball on middle and leg, helped towards fine leg for a single. Nearly carried.

The players are back out in the middle. 35 overs left in the day. If the Windies can get a breakthrough in the first 30-45 minutes, they can enjoy a good session. It will be Kemar Roach vs Henry Nicholls first up...
... DAY 1, FINAL SESSION ...

Miguel Cummins has been the pick of the bowlers for the visiting side. He has been sharp and accurate which has resulted him in being economical as well. But there has not been much from the others. New Zealand are on the back foot a little bit due to those two wickets and Taylor is either nervous or trying to impose himself, as he flashed at quite a few before the break. Could be a Rosco special on the other side or a quick exit. Join us back at 1600 LOCAL (0300 GMT) for the final session.

The Kiwis started the session with ease, with Williamson and Raval looking in no trouble at all. Then, the Windies started to concentrate on keeping the runs in check and that resulted in the wickets. The ploy was to bowl short and around the leg stump and it worked. They need to work on the extras though, with 7 no balls already being conceded so far.
Good comeback by Windies in the latter half of the session. 86/2 in 28 overs in that session but the last 7 overs saw only 22 runs for the wickets of Raval and Williamson.
Good calling. Pushes this with soft hands down the ground and takes a quick run, eager to face the first ball of the next session. TEA ON DAY 1!
Outside off, left alone.
Full and wide outside off, Ross eases it through the covers. The ball stops near the ropes and the batsmen take three.
Short and wide outside off, Rosco slashes but misses.
Fuller again, outside off, hint of outswing, driven towards mid off.
Around off, angling in, played towards short mid-wicket.
NO BALL. 7th one of the day and add 3 wides to that. Gabriel oversteps and then bowls a rubbish ball, short in length down the leg side. Taylor ducks. The stand moves to 10.
We will have one more over before the break then...
Outside off, angling away, shouldered arms to.
Flicks this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Well, he gets a boundary but the question arises - should he have gone after that? Full and wide outside off, Taylor reaches out and blasts it through the covers for a boundary. Having lost two wickets fairly quickly, New Zealand would be better off not losing another one.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off, not perfectly timed.
Outside off, quietly left alone this time.
A length ball outside off, Taylor has a needless waft and nearly edges it behind.
KEMAR ROACH to bowl probably the final over before Tea.
And again! Similar ball, similar shot, same result.
Another length ball down the leg side, Nicholls tucks it through mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a couple.
A length ball around leg, defended to the leg side.
HENRY NICHOLLS walks in at number 5, replacing Raval. One left-hander replaces another.

OUT! Caught behind! That is a jaffa and Gabriel has his man. It is a carbon copy of his first innings dismissal in the first Test. Pitched around leg and middle, Raval looks to defend but the ball just moves away off the seam and takes the outside edge. Just about carries to Dowrich who is jubilant on taking the catch. Poor Raval - misses out on a ton. He was playing for the break and got a beauty.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, left alone.
WIDE. Ridiculous tactic. It is okay to bowl short stuff but you cannot always be short, short and short. This is a long hop but Raval prefers to duck. Too high and signalled a wide.
A short ball around middle, rising steeply, RT hops and defends it towards cover.
WIDE. That is four in a row and that is too high as well. Another bouncer, another duck.
Another bouncer, meaningless one as well, Taylor does the same as to what he did on the previous ball.
A short ball down the leg side, Rosco looks to tuck it away but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards leg slip who does well to stop it to his right.
A meaningless bouncer, down the leg side, ducked under.
On a good length, around off, Ross defends.
A short ball down the leg side, Taylor cannot get it away.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a single. Gets off the mark.
The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.

NOT OUT. The answer to both queries asked in the insert below are NO. The plan does seem to be getting batsmen caught down the leg side though. This is a half volley on the pads, a scoring opportunity but perhaps Raval is playing for the break. He is late on his flick and the ball goes off something to the keeper. Dowrich appeals confidently but Gabriel just joins as an afterthought. Umpire Oxenford does not give it and Dowrich convinces his skipper to go for the review. Hot Spot shows a mark when the ball hits the pads while Snickometer shows a spike at the same moment. Nothing when the ball is near the bat. One review lost.
Howzzat? Have the Windies got another one caught down the leg side? Has Jeet Raval missed out on a ton? Brathwaite wants to have a second look. The on-field decision is not out.
Goes back in his crease and blocks it to the leg side.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
SHANNON GABRIEL is back on.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Full and outside off, driven straight towards mid off.
NO BALL. This is for the third bouncer of the over. Taylor ducks.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
On middle and leg, short in length, tucked straight to short leg.
ROSS TAYLOR walks in at number 4, replacing Williamson.

OUT! Caught down the leg side! The plan to stifle Williamson has worked. He has this tendency to walk across his stumps and the Windies were trying to make him play that tuck shot towards fine leg and in the process, edge one behind. He does so, on this occasion. There is a noise as the ball goes past and the players appeal. Umpire Tucker asks his partner whether that carried and on getting the affirmative as an answer, raises his finger. Williamson does not bother to review and walks back with a sheepish smile instead. End of an 89-run stand and Cummins has got 2 wickets on a non-responsive pitch.
NO BALL again. Short and down the leg side, Kane lets it be. Another overstepping from Cummins.
NO BALL! Too short a delivery, could have been wided, but instead it is no-balled as Cummins overstepped.
A bouncer, way over Williamson's head, he ducks comfortably.
Now MIGUEL CUMMINS is given the ball. Seems like he wanted to bowl from this end.
Throws it up to the batsman, Raval comes forward and blocks.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller and outside off, pushed straight to point.
Short and outside off, cut towards point for a single.
MIGUEL CUMMINS is back on. Wait. Cummins is handed his cap back. KRAIGG BRATHWAITE to bowl instead.

FOUR! What a shot. Floated outside off, Raval comes forward and drives it through cover-point for consecutive boundaries! Moves to 83 now, just 17 short of his century. Also, this is his 15TH boundary of this innings! 150 IS UP FOR NEW ZEALAND AS WELL.

EDGED, FOUR! Was that a chance? A missed one, for sure! Cannot totally blame the fielder. This was bowled short and outside off and Raval went back to cut. Seeing that, Shai Hope, the first slip fielder, moved instinctly to his left. But then, the ball took the outside edge and went to his right. Shai was late in reacting and the ball went through to the third man fence. The stand is worth 82 now.
Outside off, pushed to the off side.
Full and outside off, Jeet pushes hard at it and gets a bit of an outside edge towards point.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Raval lunges to defend.
Landed on a length, defended solidly.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
A short ball outside off, tapped to the off side.

FOUR! BEAUTY! That is a Williamson classic. Half volley, around off and middle, Williamson comes forward and drives it straight down the ground, past the stumps at the other end and towards the long on fence! Moves to 42 now.

Nips back in a long way from outside off, Williamson is beaten for pace and is hit on the thigh pads. Roach puts in a belated appeal for LBW but is not greeted with acceptance. Going down leg, one would think.
On a length around off, angling in, tucked towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Too much air, too full, does not land the ball at all, Raval comes forward and eases it through mid on for a boundary!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Full and on the pads, flicked through mid-wicket for three runs.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

FOUR! This has been an exhibition of mixing caution with aggression to perfection from the young man. Roach opts to bowl a slower delivery on a fullish length outside off, Raval reads it correctly, leans forward and drives it elegantly through mid off for a boundary.
On a length, defended solidly off the back foot.

FOUR! Calm and assured in approach. Genuine half volley outside off, Raval crouches and places it towards backward point. The fielder from short third man runs to his left and puts in a dive but the ball goes past him and races to the fence.
Roach goes wider of the crease and bowls a tight length on off. Jeet has it covered and defends it down the track.
Back of a length ball on off, Raval camps back and defends it in a compact manner.
Strides forward to the flighted delivery and blocks it with authority.

FOUR! Elegance and class written all over that stroke! Williamson is so assured about his foot movement and controls the length to perfection. Spots that the delivery is looped up outside off. He strides forward confidently and creams it through covers. Away she whistles to the fence. That was delightful to watch.
Eases this one confidently with the turn to deepish mid off. A run taken.
Coming in with the arm, skidding after pitching. Raval rocks back but gets a little hurried. Manages to punch it out in the end.
Tossed up around off, Raval lunges forward in defense.
Loopy delivery outside off, played with soft hands past the cover region for an easy single.

Time for drinks. New Zealand continue to control the proceedings. Jeet Raval and Kane Williamson have been circumspect in approach after lunch and are putting up a good show of class and determination. The Windies bowlers have tried hard but to no success. They need a moment of inspiration to turn things around. Perhaps, they need to work on their body language and mindset which has been pretty bland so far.
Hangs back to the back of the length delivery and blocks it right under his eyes.
No ball! Shannon Gabriel's love affair with overstepping continues. He has again missed his mark by a long way. He is tiring now. Around the pads, tucked around the corner for a single.
On a driving length outside off, Williamson is not the one to fall prey to a false shot. He plants his front foot across and makes a good leave.
Similar delivery, caressed through covers for a brace.
Fullish delivery around off, Kane strides forward and defends it confidently.

No ball! Gabriel oversteps for the first time in the game. Always expected this to be coming. Puts in that extra yard on that delivery and hits the deck hard. It shoots off the track and Williamson ducks under it. Well, the replays show that Gabriel's front foot has gone ahead of the popping crease by a country mile.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, Williamson drives it to deepish mid off. Watches his foot movement after he played that shot.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Williamson plays it with an angled blade to gully.
Chase drags his length back. Kane makes good use of the depth of the crease and buries it into the track.
Loopy delivery, Williamson comes forward and stonewalls it.
Prods forward with confidence and defends it with the spin to short leg.
Fullish delivery, placed to mid on.
Turning in sharply from a short length outside off, Williamson adjusts in his crease and blocks it besides the pitch on the leg side.
Slow through the air around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Fullish delivery outside off, Raval leans forward and pushes it to covers.
Stays well-balanced and clips it nicely to mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down. Full length delivery around leg stump, swinging in. Raval tries to flick it across but seems to have got a thick inside edge on his pads. A casual query from the Windies is turned down by the umpire. The replays confirm there was a fat edge.
Back of a length delivery outside off, played with soft hands towards gully. The slip fielder moves to his left and slides to stop it.
Straying down the leg side, helped to fine leg for a single.
A fraction short in length, cut away with the spin to the man at point.
Fullish delivery on middle, knocked to deepish mid on for an easy run.
Sits deep in the crease and places it behind point for a single.
Prods forward to defend this one but gets it off the outer half towards point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, spinning away. Raval lets it go.

A bit of delay. A short leg is coming in place. He gets his pads on. The Kiwi players have also been halting play at times to have drinks. It shouldn't be done on a regular basis. Just doesn't reflect well upon a side. Meanwhile, Roston Chase to roll his arm over now.
Another bouncer, Williamson ducks under it.
Short delivery in line of the stumps, Williamson shows good technique and sits under the bumper.
Full length delivery, sliding down the leg side. Williamson gets a little off-balanced and misses his flick. Did that brush the pad in its way to the keeper? The replays confirm so.
Fuller in length outside off, the Kiwi skipper lets it through.
Short of a length delivery outside off, shaping in. Williamson makes good use of the depth of the crease and blocks it right under his eyes.
Well played. Full delivery around off, Raval just times it past the bowler and towards mid off. The fielder is standing deep and hence, a run results.
Good length ball on off, Kane again shuffles and taps it to covers. Shouts wait on to his partner.
Fuller in length, Kane strokes it to covers.
Defense at its best. On a length around off, Williamson shuffles a touch and defends it with a straight bat. Offered the sticker's name for all to see.
No ball! That's the first one of the game, it is Cummins who has overstepped. Good length delivery around the leg stump, Raval hops and places it to fine leg to collect a run.
Similar delivery, same shot, same result.
On a length in line of the stumps, tucked from within the crease to mid-wicket.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Full delivery on middle, eased off the front foot to mid on.
FOUR! Didn't try to hit it too hard, just caressed it with timing. Full length ball outside off, Raval strides forward and strokes it through covers to find the ropes.

Where was Raval going? Misjudgement from him. He drives this past the outstretched left arm of Gabriel and takes off for a run. The mid on fielder is alert to it and gets across to his right quickly. The opener is rightly sent back by his skipper.
Good length delivery well outside off, left alone.
Fullish delivery, angling in from around the wicket. Raval comes forward and taps it to mid off.
100 up for New Zealand! Good going for the home side. Length delivery around the hips, Raval hops and tucks it in front of square leg for a brace.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl again.
Another sharp short delivery around off, Williamson ducks under it in a jiffy.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Well-directed bouncer on leg stump, Raval goes for a half-hearted pull. Miscues it but gets it over the short leg fielder and towards deep square leg. Reifer moves to his left and does the mopping up. A single taken.
In the zone outside off, Raval makes a third leave in a row. He has been really disciplined today. Has seen off the deliveries in the probing channel and has made the bowlers work hard.
Back of a length delivery, hits the deck and seams away a long way. Jeet has nothing to do with it.
On a driving length, swinging away. Raval resists the temptation to go for the drive and lets it go through safely.

Good shot but for no runs. Back of a length delivery around off, Williamson sits on the back foot and punches it sweetly to mid off. The temptation was there to go for the pull shot but opted to play it straight.
Going away with the angle, Williamson points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Back of a length delivery on off, defended compactly from within the crease.
This one is wide outside off and Kane doesn't fiddle with it.
Full length delivery, close to the off stump. Williamson puts his head down and defends it calmly.
This is good stuff from the debutant. Back of a length delivery angling across Williamson. Doesn't rise as much as the batsman expects. Kane goes for a hard slash but misses.
Around the hips, tucked around the corner for a run.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Nicely done. Fuller in length on leg stump, Kane clips it with good balance past short leg. A brace added.
Good length delivery, angling in substantially. Williamson is early into his tuck shot and hence, gets a soft leading edge which rolls down the track.
Overpitched outside off, driven elegantly to the extra cover region to rotate strike.
Swinging away from around off, Raval plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
Miguel Cummins returns for a bowl. He has been the most impressive of bowlers so far. Can he provide another breakthrough?
Pretty harmless delivery outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect. Two consecutive maidens.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a length on off, Kane has the line covered and answers it with a straight bat.
Leans forward to the fullish delivery and taps it with an open bat face to point.
In the channel outside off, the Kiwi skipper remains circumspect in approach.
Full length delivery well outside off, Williamson allows it through.
Wide outside off, not making the batsman play enough. Left alone with ease.
Good length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays back to the good length delivery and taps it to gully.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Wide outside off, Jeet lets it go.
Tight run! On a length outside off, dabbed towards covers. Raval calls for the run and his partner responds. There is a shy at the bowler's end which misses but Raval is safe anyway.

FOUR! 6th Test fifty for Jeet Raval! Well played, young man. The sparse crowd acknowledges his effort, he has played a determined knock so far. Back of a length delivery and room on offer, Raval guides it deftly through the vacant short third man region. The fielder from backward point gives it a chase, loses balance near the ropes, tries to stop the ball but fails to do so. Ends up tumbling down near the advertisement board.
Another one outside off, Jeet doesn't feel for it.

Scott Styris makes a good point on air. The edges aren't really flying to the slip cordon. Most of the times, the keeper determines where the slip fielders should stand. Sometimes the keepers like to stand a bit deep but you need to make those adjustments to create more chances.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Full delivery on middle, played with soft hands to mid on.
In the zone outside off, swinging away. Raval lets it go.
Around leg stump, tucked towards short fine leg.

Nervy! Length delivery in the zone of apprehension, straightens a bit after landing. Williamson pokes at it and gets an outside edge but the ball falls well short of Brathwaite at second slip. The edges haven't carried as the batsmen have played them with soft hands. Perhaps the slip fielders should come in close.
A bit tentative is Kane Williamson! Roach goes wider of the crease and angles it in from a good length. Williamson tries to tuck it to the leg side but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and blocks it solidly.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.

Good fielding! Well-directed bouncer on middle and leg, Raval pulls it in a controlled manner through square leg. Raymon Reifer sprints to his left, picks it up with his left hand and returns an accurate throw to the keeper. He stopped the couple due to his quickness across the turf. A run taken.
Kemar Roach to steam in from the other end.
Well bowled and equally well played! Good length delivery in the off stump channel, Williamson knows where his off stump is and watches the ball zip through to the keeper.
Fractionally overpitched around off, Williamson is looking in good touch as he drives it to Roach at deepish mid off.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Williamson has it covered and defends it with a straight bat.
Full length delivery outside off, placed with the angle to the man at covers.
On a length around off, Williamson comes forward confidently and taps it to point.
Starts off with a half volley on off, Raval drives it crisply towards mid on. Roach sprints to his left and dives to make a partial stop. A run taken.

We are back for the afternoon session. The need of the hour for the Windies is wickets. Not sure how they will get them but they need to devise a way to do so. Kane Williamson and Jeet Raval to continue their innings. Raymon Reifer to continue his spell. Two slips in place. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Miguel Cummins has been the standout bowler. He has bowled in probing channels and induced false strokes. Latham was looking jittery against him and he caught him wanting with a short delivery. That was the only reward for the visitors. The Kiwi skipper has come in and looked fluent while Raval has been solid as a rock at the other end. With not much assistance from the conditions, a tough day awaits the tourists unless they get their act together. Join us in a while for the second session.

A morning which has completely belonged to the home side. The stand-in skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite opted to field first on a greenish wicket but his bowlers haven't been up to the mark. Agreed that there wasn't much movement on offer but you need to make the batsmen play with the brand new ball. Tom Latham and Jeet Raval got off to a positive start due to some poor bowling especially from Gabriel. He bowled too many boundary balls and was rightly dealt with. Roach also bowled wide lines and didn't create much opportunities.
Fullish delivery on off, Raval strides forward to push it through covers but gets it off the inner half to square leg. A run taken. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Full delivery in line of the stumps, eased off the front foot to mid on.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Coming in with the angle, tucked around the corner for an easy single.
Full delivery wide outside off, Kane doesn't flirt with it.

Brilliant effort from Roston Chase! Such an effort can lift the morale of the entire side which is lacking confidence at the moment. Back of a length delivery, sits up nicely for Williamson. He stays well-balanced and punches it nicely to the cover region. Chase dives full length to his left to save a certain boundary. His effort is lauded by his teammates.
Length delivery outside off, pushed with soft hands to point.
Angling away from Raval who doesn't flay at it.
Good length delivery around off, defended off the back foot besides the pitch on the leg side.

Great technique displayed by Raval! For all the youngsters following the game, this is the way you should defend. Full length delivery around off, Raval strides forward and defends it with a high elbow. His head position was on the spot, right towards the ball.
Length delivery on off, Raval hangs back and answers it with a straight bat.
Good stop! Overpitched delivery on middle, Raval drives it sweetly towards Reifer who is quick to react and stops it.
Well outside off, the Kiwi skippers lets it be.
Full length ball, shaping in. Kane puts his head down and defends it calmly.

Edged but safe! Roach goes wider of the crease and angles it on a length around off. Williamson plants his front foot towards the line of the delivery and feels for it. Gets an outside edge that flies towards the slip cordon but falls well short of the fielders.
An extra man at covers now, three in total.
Fuller in length well outside off, driven with an open bat face past point to rotate strike.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length ball outside off, Raval makes an assured leave.
Kemar Roach returns for a burst.
Outside off, ignored by the Kiwi skipper.

A bit of confusion in the running! Back of a length delivery around off, Williamson punches it firmly towards covers. He takes off but hesitates a bit before eventually continuing. The fielder from the same region hares after it and keeps it down to a brace. The replays show that the fielder was lazy in getting across in the first instance. Poor fielding from the Windies.
A tad fuller, on a drivable length. Kane doesn't fall for the bait and remains circumspect in approach.
Similar delivery, left alone.
Shaping away, Kane shoulders his arms to it.
On a length around off, slanting further away. Williamson plants his front foot across and makes a good leave.
Full delivery once again, eased down the ground for an easy run. Gabriel continues to be expensive, 9 from that over.
FOUR! Gabriel is searching for some swing but there is none on offer. Low full toss around off, Williamson strokes it past the non-striker to pick up another boundary.
Very full outside off, Kane digs it out.
Full delivery around off, driven to mid off.

FOUR! The change in field doesn't bring a change in fortune. If you keep bowling such bad deliveries, you will be hit around the park. Overpitched around off, Williamson puts a confident stride forward and creams it past Gabriel. It speeds past mid off and races to the fence.
Gabriel's front foot slipped while he delivered the previous ball. The sawdust is being adjusted on the popping crease. Meanwhile, another gully comes in place. Two gullies now.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven sweetly to covers.
Shannon Gabriel is back on. He will be operating from the other end. Will it help him bowl better?
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Low full toss outside off, Williamson leans into it and strokes it past the diving fielder at extra cover for a boundary.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, Williamson comes forward and defends it with a high elbow.
Angling away, dabbed with an open face to short third man.
Full length ball on off, driven crisply to mid off.
Nicely bowled! On a length on off stump, continuing with the angle. Williamson is unsure about it and feels for it but gets beaten. Just shows the importance of putting the ball in the right areas.
Dug in short, Raval ducks under it and evades it easily.
Short of a length delivery, punched off the back foot towards covers for an easy run.
Hangs back and plays it with an angled blade to short third man.
That's a peach! Good length ball in the zone of apprehension, shapes away just a bit after hitting the deck. Good enough to beat the tentative poke from Williamson.
Good length delivery outside off, tapped with the angle to point.
Williamson is off the mark! Fullish delivery, angling in. Williamson clips it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Another one outside off and it is left alone. Maiden on debut for Reifer but he needs to bowl better lines and lengths.
Length delivery outside off, swinging away. Raval lets it through.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bowls it way outside off, Raval is no mood to flirt with that one.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Jeet doesn't fiddle with it.
Not the ideal delivery to kickstart your international career! Nerves on display. Bowls it wide outside off on a length,  Raval lets it go.

Kane Williamson comes out to bat. The skipper was a bit lazy in the first game. He will look to come back into his elements. Meanwhile, Raymon Reifer comes into the attack. Can the debutant impress in his first international outing?

OUT! The short ball gets the wicket eventually! Cummins gives the breakthrough. Finally some respite for the Windies after a lackluster first hour. Cummins steams in and hits the deck hard around leg stump and generates good bounce off the track. Latham is a bit tucked up but still goes through with the hook shot. Seems like he ends up getting some glove on it. Dowrich moves to his right and takes a regulation catch. The visitors roar in appeal but the umpire does not raise his finger. However, he does so after a while but that is probably because the batsman starts to walk. The Hot Spot confirms that it came off the glove. The opener has had his issues with the short ball and falls prey to it. The steady 65-run stand comes to an end.
Fullish in length, blocked watchfully.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Nicely controllled! Short ball around leg stump, Latham gets on top of the bounce and pulls it with authority behind square on the leg side. No protection in the deep and the ball races to the fence.
Angling in, played to mid-wicket.
Full length delivery in line of the stumps, driven crisply to mid on.
Comes forward to the tossed up delivery and blocks it.

FOUR! Almost a caught and bowled off a poor delivery! Low full toss on off, Raval drives it to the right side of Chase. The bowler is a little late to react, hangs his right hand out but the ball goes past him in a flash and rolls to the fence.
Loopy delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Prods forward and taps it with the spin to point.
Camps back to the shorter delivery and stonewalls it.
FOUR! Nice use of the feet. Raval is growing in confidence. Tossed up ball around off, Raval skips down the track and chips it over mid off to find the fence.

Almost chops it back! Short of a length ball, around off. Latham pushes at it with hard hands but gets a thick inside edge towards the pitch on the leg side. A testing over from Cummins comes to an end.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Latham has looked a bit jittery in this over. Cummins runs in and hits the deck hard. Extracts good bounce as well. Latham is caught in a tangle, looks to fend it away but gets an inside edge near his stomach area.
Short of a length in that off stump zone, Tom hangs back and answers it with a straight bat this time.
This is better from Cummins. Keeps it straight and makes the batsman play. Back of a length on off, moving in after pitching. Latham hangs back and fends it off tentatively.
Cummins runs in from over the wicket and bowls it in the channel around off. Latham hangs deep in the crease and lets it sail through in the gloves of the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Coming in with the arm, kept out watchfully.

Uppish but safe! A bit of drift on that one, around the leg stump. Raval kneels for the sweep but gets a top edge. The ball balloons over the keeper and falls safely near the vacant short fine leg region. Two runs taken.
Loopy ball on middle, Raval strides forward and blocks it stoutly.

FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Short outside off, Raval waits for it and dabs it through the short third man region. The fielder from backward point gives it a hard chase but only comes second best. With that, the 50-run stand is up between the duo. It has been a walk in the park for them so far.
Slow through the air, Jeet prods forward in defense.
Third leave in a row. Back of a length delivery, seaming away after hitting the deck. Latham doesn't fiddle with it.
Good length delivery, slanting across Latham. He points his bat skywards to allow it through.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

Close shave! Just short of first slip. On a length around off, slanting away after pitching. Latham pokes at it but gets an outside edge. Shane Dowrich doesn't go for a dive as it is quite far away from him. Kieran Powell at first slip lines it up but it falls about half a meter short of him. He played that with soft hands and hence, it didn't carry. Hard to blame the keeper for not going for it.
On a length around off, Tom eases it off the front foot to covers.
Fuller in length around off, Latham strides forward and strokes it nicely to mid off.
Slow turn on that occasion. Floated outside off, spinning away. Raval plants his front foot across and lets it through safely.
Chase drags his length back and bowls it around off, Raval hangs back and defends it solidly to covers.
Erring on the leg stump line, the batsman drives it crisply to the fielder at mid on.
Similar delivery, Raval puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Slow through the air on off, Jeet lunges forward in defense.
Starts off with a fullish delivery on off, Raval pushes it off the front foot to mid on.

DRINKS BREAK. No rocket science. It has been the hour for the Kiwis. Not much seam movement, not much swing movement, not much good bowling, not much good fielding. A buffet on the cards. Feast yourself. Seems like Brathwaite has misread the pitch.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Full and outside off, Jeet drives it through the covers where skipper Brathwaite dives but is unable to stop the ball. Almost as a punishment, the cherry stops near the boundary. Poor Brathwaite, with no one near him, has to himself go running to fetch the ball, all the way to the boundary. Three runs taken.
Gets tighter in line and defends.
FOUR! Not quite in control. A length ball outside off, Raval plays away from his body and the ball flies off the outside edge behind point and races to the fence.

DROPPED? Tough chance any which ways. The ploy nearly works. Banged in short, around leg, Latham looks to pull but is unable to control the shot. He is unable to control the bounce as well and miscues it towards the leg side. Shimron Hetmyer at leg gully reacts well but is too close for the catch. The ball hits his fingers and goes through to backward square leg. A single taken. Tough to call that a chance.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Excuse me? Asks Raval. Forget what happened on the previous ball. Let us live in the present. He gets beaten on the last delivery but is pretty much focussed on this one. Sees the length short and picks it up in a trice. Off he swivels on the back foot and plays a Nataraja pull shot through mid-wicket. Raval moves to 21 with his 4th boundary.

EDGED! But short. The first false shot which produces an edge. Roach keeps his length as full, then makes it to move away. Jeet is a bit late in playing that and gets an outside edge. However, he plays that with soft hands and hence, the ball does not carry to third slip.
Full again, slightly tempting to be driven but Jeet is not falling for it. Just lets it go.
Full again, holding its line outside off, watchfully let through again.
Full and outside off, left alone watchfully.

Raval has exhibited good technique to play the fast bowlers. It is hard to criticize such a confident player but in terms of the modern age, he needs to develop the habit of rotating the strike. There are plenty of gaps available on the field and apart from that first single which he took ages ago, Jeet hasn't looked interested in running. He is either defending or dealing in boundaries.
A short ball, around middle and off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A bouncer but well over his head, Raval ducks.
On a good length around leg, Raval gets on top of the bounce and defends the ball back to the bowler.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A length ball outside off, left alone.
Oh dear. That is miles outside off, Tom has nothing to do with it. Surprisingly, it is not wided.
Full and around off, Latham waits for the ball to come to him and then dabs it towards the slip cordon.
Yawn. Same thing again and again. Nice to be consistent but he needs to make the batsman play.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Goes wider outside off, let through again.
Landed outside off, pretty wide, left alone.
Change of ends for KEMAR ROACH.
One more leave outside off to end the over.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
WIDE. A bouncer, too high, outside leg, Raval ducks and it is wided.
A leg gully comes in now. Expect some short stuff.
A length ball and pretty straight, watchfully defended.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
MIGUEL CUMMINS comes in as the first change of the morning.
On the pads, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
The batsman has played it to the point region.

FOUR! AWESOME! Sixth boundary of the morning. Full and around off, Latham comes forward and drives it exquisitely down the ground. There is no mid off but even if there was one, he was going to come second.
A nice yorker, but it is outside off. Could have been left alone but Latham decides to play and digs it out towards cover.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
A length ball outside off, allowed to go through.
One more leave outside off to end the over.
Landed outside off, left alone.

FOUR! That is not a bad ball but what a good shot. A short ball, around middle, generates nice bounce but Raval comfortably sits on top of the bounce and pulls it through mid-wicket. Again, stressing that it was not that bad a ball but Raval made it look pretty easy.
Good length ball, around off, Jeet pushes at it tentatively and gets it off the outer half to gully.
Outside off, angling further away, let through.
A length ball around off, Raval trusts the bounce and lets it through.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. First maiden for Gabriel.
Fuller, flicked straight to mid-wicket again.
On middle and off, watchfully defended towards short mid-wicket.
Similar ball to the previous one, left alone again.
Outside off, gets it to come back in but is too far to be played, Latham lets it go.
On a good length around middle, watchfully defended.
